articles.title: GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control rooms, 55 rehabilitation centres readied
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: With Cyclone Akvan approaching, the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) has sounded an alert and put its entire civic machinery on standby to tackle any eventuality arising from heavy rainfall and strong winds. The civic body has put in place extensive arrangements for emergency response, rescue, relief and restoration operations to minimise inconvenience to the public.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: GVMC Additional Commissioner S.S. Varma said that 11 control rooms had been established across the city to provide round-the-clock emergency services and respond to public complaints. Special personnel had been deployed in three shifts at the City Operations Centre (COC) at the GVMC headquarters to receive complaints and coordinate immediate relief measures. Residents can contact the GVMC control room at 180042500009 or send their complaints and requests for assistance through WhatsApp at 9014218870. As many as 55 low-lying areas across the city have been identified as vulnerable, and special monitoring arrangements have been made in these locations. The civic body has also kept 55 rehabilitation centres ready to accommodate residents who may have to be evacuated to safer locations depending on the situation. Mr. Varma appealed to people living in low-lying and hilly areas to remain vigilant and follow the instructions issued by the authorities. Residents were advised to move to safer places whenever required and remain cautious until the impact of the cyclone subsided. The GVMC has also kept a substantial fleet of machinery and vehicles ready to deal with emergencies such as fallen trees, waterlogging and road obstructions. The equipment available for relief and restoration operations includes 30 JCBs, 70 tippers, 30 mini excavators and 10 oil engines. In addition, 15 special teams have been constituted under the Horticulture Department to clear uprooted trees and branches from roads. Each team comprises a tipper, two power saws and four personnel. The teams have been strategically deployed across the Madhurawada, East, South, North, West, Gajuwaka and Pendurthi areas to ensure a quick response. For sanitation management and emergency operations, the civic body has constituted 98 Rapid Response Teams, one for each of the city’s 98 wards. Each team comprises 15 personnel and will take up the removal of stagnant rainwater, sanitation works and other emergency activities during and after the cyclone. 📰 GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control rooms, 55 rehabilitation centres readied

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:27:26 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: With Cyclone Akvan approaching, the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) has sounded an alert and put its entire civic machinery on standby to tackle any eventuality arising from heavy rainfall and strong winds. The civic body has put in place extensive arrangements for emergency response, rescue, relief and restoration operations to minimise inconvenience to the public.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: GVMC Additional Commissioner S.S. Varma said that 11 control rooms had been established across the city to provide round-the-clock emergency services and respond to public complaints. Special personnel had been deployed in three shifts at the City Operations Centre (COC) at the GVMC headquarters to receive complaints and coordinate immediate relief measures. Residents can contact the GVMC control room at 180042500009 or send their complaints and requests for assistance through WhatsApp at 9014218870. As many as 55 low-lying areas across the city have been identified as vulnerable, and special monitoring arrangements have been made in these locations. The civic body has also kept 55 rehabilitation centres ready to accommodate residents who may have to be evacuated to safer locations depending on the situation. Mr. Varma appealed to people living in low-lying and hilly areas to remain vigilant and follow the instructions issued by the authorities. Residents were advised to move to safer places whenever required and remain cautious until the impact of the cyclone subsided. The GVMC has also kept a substantial fleet of machinery and vehicles ready to deal with emergencies such as fallen trees, waterlogging and road obstructions. The equipment available for relief and restoration operations includes 30 JCBs, 70 tippers, 30 mini excavators and 10 oil engines. In addition, 15 special teams have been constituted under the Horticulture Department to clear uprooted trees and branches from roads. Each team comprises a tipper, two power saws and four personnel. The teams have been strategically deployed across the Madhurawada, East, South, North, West, Gajuwaka and Pendurthi areas to ensure a quick response. For sanitation management and emergency operations, the civic body has constituted 98 Rapid Response Teams, one for each of the city’s 98 wards. Each team comprises 15 personnel and will take up the removal of stagnant rainwater, sanitation works and other emergency activities during and after the cyclone. The GVMC has also identified eight vulnerable electricity poles and is coordinating with officials of the concerned electricity department to take necessary preventive measures.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Stating that coordinated efforts were being made to tackle any eventuality, the Additional Commissioner said the GVMC was working in close coordination with the District Revenue Administration, APEPDCL and the Fire Services Department. Joint arrangements had been made to respond promptly to power supply disruptions, fallen trees and road blockages.

articles.title: Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental health centres despite protests by psychiatrists, doctors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: GO issued renaming Mental Health Centres as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Keralam government has gone ahead with its decision to rename the Mental Health Centres (MHCs) in the State as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness”, even after the pitfalls of such a move was pointed out by psychiatry professionals and other professional bodies of doctors. With the government issuing the government order (GO) on November 13, formalising the change in nomenclature, the Indian Psychiatric Society’s (IPS) Keralam branch and other medical bodies, including the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and the Kerala Government Medical Officers’ Association, have renewed their warning that the change in nomenclature could undermine the clinical, academic and legal identity of the State’s MHCs. Mental health professionals in the State have yet again pointed out to the government that the nomenclature, Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness, was one that trivialised the legitimacy and seriousness of a branch of modern medicine which dealt with the treatment of serious mental health disorders. The controversy follows a suggestion by a Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on August 21, 2026, that the government consider renaming the centres to address the stigma associated with them. The court had suggested the name “Institutes of Behavioural Management”. With the IMA and the IPS Kerala approaching the High Court with their objections, the court had asked the government to hold consultations with the medical professionals on the issues they had brought up. Accordingly, the Keralam branch of the Indian Psychiatric Society and the IMA had met the Health department officials, including the Principal Secretary (Health), on September 16 and had proposed “Regional Institutes of Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences” as the best option if the government was keen on renaming the MHCs. However, despite the concerns expressed by the medical professionals about the repercussions of renaming medical institutions to resemble the names of spas or the so-called holistic treatment centres that are a dime a dozen in the State, the government was apparently unwilling to drop the ‘happiness and wellness' tag, and chose to rename MHCs as Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness. The psychiatrists have urged the government to reconsider the decision, arguing that replacing the established terms “mental health” and “psychiatry” with “happiness and wellness” would neither address the stigma associated with mental illness nor reflect the specialised treatment provided by these institutions. They have pointed out that happiness and wellness are broad concepts that do not adequately convey the purpose of a specialised psychiatric treatment facility.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a statement issued on November 17, the IPS pointed out that the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, and the statutory bodies established under it use the term “mental health.”

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental health centres despite protests by psychiatrists, doctors

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:14:20 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: GO issued renaming Mental Health Centres as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Keralam government has gone ahead with its decision to rename the Mental Health Centres (MHCs) in the State as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness”, even after the pitfalls of such a move was pointed out by psychiatry professionals and other professional bodies of doctors. With the government issuing the government order (GO) on November 13, formalising the change in nomenclature, the Indian Psychiatric Society’s (IPS) Keralam branch and other medical bodies, including the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and the Kerala Government Medical Officers’ Association, have renewed their warning that the change in nomenclature could undermine the clinical, academic and legal identity of the State’s MHCs. Mental health professionals in the State have yet again pointed out to the government that the nomenclature, Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness, was one that trivialised the legitimacy and seriousness of a branch of modern medicine which dealt with the treatment of serious mental health disorders. The controversy follows a suggestion by a Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on August 21, 2026, that the government consider renaming the centres to address the stigma associated with them. The court had suggested the name “Institutes of Behavioural Management”. With the IMA and the IPS Kerala approaching the High Court with their objections, the court had asked the government to hold consultations with the medical professionals on the issues they had brought up. Accordingly, the Keralam branch of the Indian Psychiatric Society and the IMA had met the Health department officials, including the Principal Secretary (Health), on September 16 and had proposed “Regional Institutes of Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences” as the best option if the government was keen on renaming the MHCs. However, despite the concerns expressed by the medical professionals about the repercussions of renaming medical institutions to resemble the names of spas or the so-called holistic treatment centres that are a dime a dozen in the State, the government was apparently unwilling to drop the ‘happiness and wellness' tag, and chose to rename MHCs as Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness. The psychiatrists have urged the government to reconsider the decision, arguing that replacing the established terms “mental health” and “psychiatry” with “happiness and wellness” would neither address the stigma associated with mental illness nor reflect the specialised treatment provided by these institutions. They have pointed out that happiness and wellness are broad concepts that do not adequately convey the purpose of a specialised psychiatric treatment facility.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a statement issued on November 17, the IPS pointed out that the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, and the statutory bodies established under it use the term “mental health.”

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।

Professional (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Professional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Psychiatric' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Association (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Association' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental health centres despite protests by psychiatrists, doctors", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. GO issued renaming Mental Health Centres as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental healt' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental he' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental he' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "GO issued renaming Mental Health Centres as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Keralam govt. issues order renaming mental health centres despite protests by psychiatrists, doctors"?

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "In a statement issued on November 17, the IPS pointed out that the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, and the statutory bodies established under it use the..." (Hinglish Arth: 17 नवंबर को जारी एक बयान में, आईपीएस ने बताया कि मानसिक स्वास्थ्य देखभाल अधिनियम, 2017 और इसके तहत स्थापित वैधानिक निकाय "मानसिक स्वास्थ्य" शब्द का उपयोग करते हैं।)

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: GO issued renaming Mental Health Centres as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Keralam government has gone ahead with its decision to rename the Mental Health Centres (MHCs) in the State as “Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness”, even after the pitfalls of such a move was pointed out by psychiatry professionals and other professional bodies of doctors. With the government issuing the government order (GO) on November 13, formalising the change in nomenclature, the Indian Psychiatric Society’s (IPS) Keralam branch and other medical bodies, including the Indian Medical Association (IMA) and the Kerala Government Medical Officers’ Association, have renewed their warning that the change in nomenclature could undermine the clinical, academic and legal identity of the State’s MHCs. Mental health professionals in the State have yet again pointed out to the government that the nomenclature, Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness, was one that trivialised the legitimacy and seriousness of a branch of modern medicine which dealt with the treatment of serious mental health disorders. The controversy follows a suggestion by a Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on August 21, 2026, that the government consider renaming the centres to address the stigma associated with them. The court had suggested the name “Institutes of Behavioural Management”. With the IMA and the IPS Kerala approaching the High Court with their objections, the court had asked the government to hold consultations with the medical professionals on the issues they had brought up. Accordingly, the Keralam branch of the Indian Psychiatric Society and the IMA had met the Health department officials, including the Principal Secretary (Health), on September 16 and had proposed “Regional Institutes of Psychiatry and Behavioural Sciences” as the best option if the government was keen on renaming the MHCs. However, despite the concerns expressed by the medical professionals about the repercussions of renaming medical institutions to resemble the names of spas or the so-called holistic treatment centres that are a dime a dozen in the State, the government was apparently unwilling to drop the ‘happiness and wellness' tag, and chose to rename MHCs as Regional Institutes of Happiness and Wellness. The psychiatrists have urged the government to reconsider the decision, arguing that replacing the established terms “mental health” and “psychiatry” with “happiness and wellness” would neither address the stigma associated with mental illness nor reflect the specialised treatment provided by these institutions. They have pointed out that happiness and wellness are broad concepts that do not adequately convey the purpose of a specialised psychiatric treatment facility.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a statement issued on November 17, the IPS pointed out that the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, and the statutory bodies established under it use the term “mental health.”

articles.title: Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical gauze in abdomen during gallbladder surgery
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the doctor guilty of gross medical negligence The case is related to the late Nibha Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) ordered a doctor, found guilty of gross negligence for leaving a surgical gauze (cotton pad) inside a patient’s abdomen during a routine gallbladder operation, to pay a compensation of ₹30 lakh. The case is related to the late Nibha Singh (aged 53), wife of Mani Kant Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar. Following complaints of abdominal pain, the deceased had consulted Dr. Rajesh Kumar Singh (Opposite Party No. 1), a laparoscopic surgeon at Gayatri Nursing Home in Saharsa. Acting on the doctor’s advice, she underwent surgery to remove her gallbladder on March 19, 2016. Post-surgery, her health began to deteriorate rapidly; she suffered from severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and a bowel obstruction. Although she was examined by several doctors and hospitals, the root cause of her condition remained unidentified. Then she was admitted to the Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in New Delhi where doctors performed an emergency surgery (laparotomy). During the procedure, a large, blood-soaked surgical gauze (sponge) measuring 15x4x3 cm—was discovered inside her abdomen, which had caused an infection (peritonitis) to spread throughout the abdominal cavity. Despite medical intervention, the patient passed away on July 1, 2016 — just hours after being discharged from the hospital — due to severe complications and the resulting infection. The bench included the President Justice Sanjay Kumar and Judicial Member Md Shamim Akhtar. Mr. Akhtar, cited previous rulings by the Supreme Court and the National Commission, clarified that leaving surgical materials or gauze inside a patient’s abdomen during an operation clearly falls under the category of ‘gross negligence.’ In its order, the Commission stated that it is the primary duty of a doctor and their surgical team to account for all surgical instruments and gauze before closing the incision; failure to do so in this instance put the patient’s life at grave risk. The Commission has directed the primary erring doctor (Opposite Party No. 1) to pay the aggrieved husband a sum of ₹30,00,000 (thirty lakh rupees) as compensation, along with ₹20,000 towards litigation costs, within 60 days of receiving the order.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Should the payment not be made within the stipulated timeframe, it will accrue interest at a rate of 8% per annum. Opposite party no.1 failed to act upon the repeated visit of patient with complain of severe abdomen pain and distention and should have prompted timely investigation using appropriate imaging modalities instead opposite party no.1 advised symptomatic medicines and failed to diagnose real cause of pain and suffering,“ the Commission observed in the order.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical gauze in abdomen during gallbladder surgery

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:06:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the doctor guilty of gross medical negligence The case is related to the late Nibha Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) ordered a doctor, found guilty of gross negligence for leaving a surgical gauze (cotton pad) inside a patient’s abdomen during a routine gallbladder operation, to pay a compensation of ₹30 lakh. The case is related to the late Nibha Singh (aged 53), wife of Mani Kant Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar. Following complaints of abdominal pain, the deceased had consulted Dr. Rajesh Kumar Singh (Opposite Party No. 1), a laparoscopic surgeon at Gayatri Nursing Home in Saharsa. Acting on the doctor’s advice, she underwent surgery to remove her gallbladder on March 19, 2016. Post-surgery, her health began to deteriorate rapidly; she suffered from severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and a bowel obstruction. Although she was examined by several doctors and hospitals, the root cause of her condition remained unidentified. Then she was admitted to the Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in New Delhi where doctors performed an emergency surgery (laparotomy). During the procedure, a large, blood-soaked surgical gauze (sponge) measuring 15x4x3 cm—was discovered inside her abdomen, which had caused an infection (peritonitis) to spread throughout the abdominal cavity. Despite medical intervention, the patient passed away on July 1, 2016 — just hours after being discharged from the hospital — due to severe complications and the resulting infection. The bench included the President Justice Sanjay Kumar and Judicial Member Md Shamim Akhtar. Mr. Akhtar, cited previous rulings by the Supreme Court and the National Commission, clarified that leaving surgical materials or gauze inside a patient’s abdomen during an operation clearly falls under the category of ‘gross negligence.’ In its order, the Commission stated that it is the primary duty of a doctor and their surgical team to account for all surgical instruments and gauze before closing the incision; failure to do so in this instance put the patient’s life at grave risk. The Commission has directed the primary erring doctor (Opposite Party No. 1) to pay the aggrieved husband a sum of ₹30,00,000 (thirty lakh rupees) as compensation, along with ₹20,000 towards litigation costs, within 60 days of receiving the order.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Should the payment not be made within the stipulated timeframe, it will accrue interest at a rate of 8% per annum. Opposite party no.1 failed to act upon the repeated visit of patient with complain of severe abdomen pain and distention and should have prompted timely investigation using appropriate imaging modalities instead opposite party no.1 advised symptomatic medicines and failed to diagnose real cause of pain and suffering,“ the Commission observed in the order.

articles.title: HC interim orders over fertility centres
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court on Wednesday directed the officials of the Medical and Health department to shift the persons under treatment at Oasis Fertility centres to IVF centres of the government. The ongoing medical treatment to those 51 persons should be continued at the government IVF centres, the judge said.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The judge passed the interim direction after hearing a writ petition filed by the Oasis Fertility centres being operated by the Sadguru Health Care Services Private Limited questioning the recent cases initiated by police accusing fertility centres of indulging in artificial insemination. The petitioner’s counsel contended that his client did not indulge in any illegal activity. The medical treatment being extended to 51 persons in the fertility centres was at different stages. If adequate precautions were not taken, the objectives of the treatment would be defeated, the counsel said. The judge instructed the government to file counter affidavits within two weeks.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a related development, Justice T. Madhavi Devi of the HC issued notices to the government in a writ petition filed by doctor Durga Rao who was facing charges of collecting sperm samples illegally. The doctor challenged the registration of multiple cases on similar charges against him. The matter was adjourned to November 23 for next hearing.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 HC interim orders over fertility centres

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:05:57 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court on Wednesday directed the officials of the Medical and Health department to shift the persons under treatment at Oasis Fertility centres to IVF centres of the government. The ongoing medical treatment to those 51 persons should be continued at the government IVF centres, the judge said.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The judge passed the interim direction after hearing a writ petition filed by the Oasis Fertility centres being operated by the Sadguru Health Care Services Private Limited questioning the recent cases initiated by police accusing fertility centres of indulging in artificial insemination. The petitioner’s counsel contended that his client did not indulge in any illegal activity. The medical treatment being extended to 51 persons in the fertility centres was at different stages. If adequate precautions were not taken, the objectives of the treatment would be defeated, the counsel said. The judge instructed the government to file counter affidavits within two weeks.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a related development, Justice T. Madhavi Devi of the HC issued notices to the government in a writ petition filed by doctor Durga Rao who was facing charges of collecting sperm samples illegally. The doctor challenged the registration of multiple cases on similar charges against him. The matter was adjourned to November 23 for next hearing.

articles.title: Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may cost EPFO ₹1.1 lakh crore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: As on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Four years after a Supreme Court judgement on provident fund pension based on higher wages, the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has said that it may have to spend an additional ₹1.109 lakh crore to implement the order and pay higher pensions to about 4.45 lakh applicants. In a communication to the Central Board of Trustees, which is meeting here on Thursday, the EPFO said it considered 15.24 lakh applications for higher pension and, as on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders (PPOs) have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners. The EPFO received 17.49 lakh applications for pension on higher wages after the Supreme Court judgment, of which 2.24 lakh applications were not forwarded by the employers till the last date of January 31, 2025. Out of around 15.24 lakh applications received by the EPFO, 99.2 per cent have been disposed of and 4,45,471 demand letters have been issued. Out of these, 80,067 cases have been found ineligible later due to non-remittance of demand amount. “Around 2,62,102 applicants have deposited the demand amount/ consent out of which 1,03,793 are continuing in service and 1,58,309 have already retired. Out of these applicants, 1,53,901 have submitted Form-10D or are already pensioners. PPOs have been issued to a total of around 1,51,874 applicants. In addition, 2,027 PPOs are under finalisation and will be issued very shortly,” the EPFO said in the communication to its trustees. The total additional liability is ₹78,501.42 crore for 3,15,601 applications. “The per-person liability is estimated at ₹25.99 lakh for active members and ₹23.14 lakh for pensioners, resulting in an overall average per-person liability of around ₹24.9 lakh across both groups,” the EPFO said. It added that till November 13, demand amount or consent has been received from 2,62,102 applicants to the joint option for which the additional proportionate liability would be approximately ₹65,263 crore. “Similarly, the estimated additional proportionate liability considering approval of 100 per cent of total applications for which demand notices have been issued (i.e., 4.454 lakh) would be about ₹1.109 lakh crore. This estimation, however, is likely to vary in case any additional set of employees, members, pensioners become eligible for any reason whatsoever, in future, particularly on account of the ongoing litigations,” the EPFO said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To resolve the delays, the EPFO has said timely Issue of PPOs and release of arrears will be implemented and all legal cases will be defended properly to ensure that there is no adverse legal consequence. It has urged the CBT to take note of the information and give directions to the EPFO on the matter.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may cost EPFO ₹1.1 lakh crore

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:05:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: As on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Four years after a Supreme Court judgement on provident fund pension based on higher wages, the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has said that it may have to spend an additional ₹1.109 lakh crore to implement the order and pay higher pensions to about 4.45 lakh applicants. In a communication to the Central Board of Trustees, which is meeting here on Thursday, the EPFO said it considered 15.24 lakh applications for higher pension and, as on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders (PPOs) have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners. The EPFO received 17.49 lakh applications for pension on higher wages after the Supreme Court judgment, of which 2.24 lakh applications were not forwarded by the employers till the last date of January 31, 2025. Out of around 15.24 lakh applications received by the EPFO, 99.2 per cent have been disposed of and 4,45,471 demand letters have been issued. Out of these, 80,067 cases have been found ineligible later due to non-remittance of demand amount. “Around 2,62,102 applicants have deposited the demand amount/ consent out of which 1,03,793 are continuing in service and 1,58,309 have already retired. Out of these applicants, 1,53,901 have submitted Form-10D or are already pensioners. PPOs have been issued to a total of around 1,51,874 applicants. In addition, 2,027 PPOs are under finalisation and will be issued very shortly,” the EPFO said in the communication to its trustees. The total additional liability is ₹78,501.42 crore for 3,15,601 applications. “The per-person liability is estimated at ₹25.99 lakh for active members and ₹23.14 lakh for pensioners, resulting in an overall average per-person liability of around ₹24.9 lakh across both groups,” the EPFO said. It added that till November 13, demand amount or consent has been received from 2,62,102 applicants to the joint option for which the additional proportionate liability would be approximately ₹65,263 crore. “Similarly, the estimated additional proportionate liability considering approval of 100 per cent of total applications for which demand notices have been issued (i.e., 4.454 lakh) would be about ₹1.109 lakh crore. This estimation, however, is likely to vary in case any additional set of employees, members, pensioners become eligible for any reason whatsoever, in future, particularly on account of the ongoing litigations,” the EPFO said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To resolve the delays, the EPFO has said timely Issue of PPOs and release of arrears will be implemented and all legal cases will be defended properly to ensure that there is no adverse legal consequence. It has urged the CBT to take note of the information and give directions to the EPFO on the matter.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Communication (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Communication' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Organisation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Organisation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may cost EPFO ₹1.1 lakh crore", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. As on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may cost ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may co' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may co' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "As on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners." (Hinglish Arth: 13 नवम्बर तक 4,45,471 आवेदकों को मांग पत्र जारी किये गये तथा 1,51,874 पेंशनभोगियों को पेंशन भुगतान आदेश जारी किये जा चुके हैं।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may cost EPFO ₹1.1 lakh crore"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. It has urged the CBT to take note of the information and give directions to the EPFO on the matter.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "It has urged the CBT to take note of the information and give directions to the EPFO on the matter." (Hinglish Arth: इसने सीबीटी से सूचना पर ध्यान देने और मामले पर ईपीएफओ को निर्देश देने का आग्रह किया है।)

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: As on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Four years after a Supreme Court judgement on provident fund pension based on higher wages, the Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has said that it may have to spend an additional ₹1.109 lakh crore to implement the order and pay higher pensions to about 4.45 lakh applicants. In a communication to the Central Board of Trustees, which is meeting here on Thursday, the EPFO said it considered 15.24 lakh applications for higher pension and, as on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders (PPOs) have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners. The EPFO received 17.49 lakh applications for pension on higher wages after the Supreme Court judgment, of which 2.24 lakh applications were not forwarded by the employers till the last date of January 31, 2025. Out of around 15.24 lakh applications received by the EPFO, 99.2 per cent have been disposed of and 4,45,471 demand letters have been issued. Out of these, 80,067 cases have been found ineligible later due to non-remittance of demand amount. “Around 2,62,102 applicants have deposited the demand amount/ consent out of which 1,03,793 are continuing in service and 1,58,309 have already retired. Out of these applicants, 1,53,901 have submitted Form-10D or are already pensioners. PPOs have been issued to a total of around 1,51,874 applicants. In addition, 2,027 PPOs are under finalisation and will be issued very shortly,” the EPFO said in the communication to its trustees. The total additional liability is ₹78,501.42 crore for 3,15,601 applications. “The per-person liability is estimated at ₹25.99 lakh for active members and ₹23.14 lakh for pensioners, resulting in an overall average per-person liability of around ₹24.9 lakh across both groups,” the EPFO said. It added that till November 13, demand amount or consent has been received from 2,62,102 applicants to the joint option for which the additional proportionate liability would be approximately ₹65,263 crore. “Similarly, the estimated additional proportionate liability considering approval of 100 per cent of total applications for which demand notices have been issued (i.e., 4.454 lakh) would be about ₹1.109 lakh crore. This estimation, however, is likely to vary in case any additional set of employees, members, pensioners become eligible for any reason whatsoever, in future, particularly on account of the ongoing litigations,” the EPFO said.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: To resolve the delays, the EPFO has said timely Issue of PPOs and release of arrears will be implemented and all legal cases will be defended properly to ensure that there is no adverse legal consequence. It has urged the CBT to take note of the information and give directions to the EPFO on the matter.

articles.title: Pioneering musician and journalist Sakuntala Narasimhan passes away
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Sakuntala Narasimhan, a trailblazing musician, journalist, feminist and consumer rights activist, passed away on November 18. She was 86.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A multifaceted personality, she had the rare distinction of being a vocalist in both Carnatic and Hindustani traditions, apart from being a journalist with two PhDs in Women’s Studies and Musicology. When her first-born was only a year or two, she mysteriously lost her voice. She could barely speak, let alone sing. The doctors failed to identify the cause. For Sakuntala, an accomplished vocalist, being confined to home with a young child and unable to sing was deeply frustrating. It was this setback that led her to take up writing, recalls her daughter, Shobhana Narasimhan, professor at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research. “A women’s magazine held a short story competition, which she won. She then got to know the people at the magazine and gradually started writing more and more,” her daughter recollected. She was a longstanding columnist for multiple newspapers. “When she got married, she was pursuing a PhD in economics. However, she couldn’t complete it because I was born a year later. It always bothered her that she didn’t have a PhD,” says Ms. Shobhana, a physicist. “When I got my PhD in 1991, I told her, “Amma, now it’s your turn.” She went ahead and got her first PhD in women’s studies and then another in musicology.” Sakuntala Narasimhan with musician Archana Udupa. | Photo Credit: File photo Renowned musician Archana Udupa, one of her students, remembers her as a genius who could do self jugalbandi, switching back and forth between Hindustani and Carnatic styles. She however, feels her teacher didn’t get the dues she deserved.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “She was the only A-top artist — A Top is more than A grade — in both All India Radio and Doordarshan, and both in Carnatic and Hindustani. I think our industry could have celebrated her even more. She got her State award when she was nearing 80. We need to celebrate such people at the right time and before it is too late.”

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Pioneering musician and journalist Sakuntala Narasimhan passes away

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:02:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Sakuntala Narasimhan, a trailblazing musician, journalist, feminist and consumer rights activist, passed away on November 18. She was 86.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A multifaceted personality, she had the rare distinction of being a vocalist in both Carnatic and Hindustani traditions, apart from being a journalist with two PhDs in Women’s Studies and Musicology. When her first-born was only a year or two, she mysteriously lost her voice. She could barely speak, let alone sing. The doctors failed to identify the cause. For Sakuntala, an accomplished vocalist, being confined to home with a young child and unable to sing was deeply frustrating. It was this setback that led her to take up writing, recalls her daughter, Shobhana Narasimhan, professor at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research. “A women’s magazine held a short story competition, which she won. She then got to know the people at the magazine and gradually started writing more and more,” her daughter recollected. She was a longstanding columnist for multiple newspapers. “When she got married, she was pursuing a PhD in economics. However, she couldn’t complete it because I was born a year later. It always bothered her that she didn’t have a PhD,” says Ms. Shobhana, a physicist. “When I got my PhD in 1991, I told her, “Amma, now it’s your turn.” She went ahead and got her first PhD in women’s studies and then another in musicology.” Sakuntala Narasimhan with musician Archana Udupa. | Photo Credit: File photo Renowned musician Archana Udupa, one of her students, remembers her as a genius who could do self jugalbandi, switching back and forth between Hindustani and Carnatic styles. She however, feels her teacher didn’t get the dues she deserved.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “She was the only A-top artist — A Top is more than A grade — in both All India Radio and Doordarshan, and both in Carnatic and Hindustani. I think our industry could have celebrated her even more. She got her State award when she was nearing 80. We need to celebrate such people at the right time and before it is too late.”

articles.title: UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has reconstituted a 10-member group that works on promoting science, technology and innovation toward achieving its Sustainable Development Goals. The lone Indian in this group is former biologist and former Council of Scientific and Industrial Research CSIR Director General, Shekhar Mande, who is also currently President, Indian National Science Academy. The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while preparing for the 2027 SDG Summit. “The group comprises distinguished experts from diverse geographic and disciplinary backgrounds from both developing and developed countries. Each member, recognised for their international excellence in science or technology, brings a wealth of experience and insight from civil society, the private sector, and the scientific community, underscoring the inclusive and comprehensive approach the UN is taking towards sustainable development,” an accompanying press statement noted. The other members of the group are Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana), Deputy Director-General of CSIR Ghana; Giorgio Rossi (Italy), Vice-President of Elettra-Sincrotrone Trieste; Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Associate Professor at Malmö University; Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Professor at the Federal University of Campina Grande; Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russia), Member of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation; Motoko Kotani (Japan), Executive Director of Science at RIKEN; Jin Li (China), President of Fudan University; Madin Maseeh (Maldives), President of the Maldives Space Research Organisation; and Rita Orji (Nigeria), Canada Research Chair in Persuasive Technology at Dalhousie University. Professor Mande is also President of Vijnana Bharti, which, along with the Ministry of Science and Technology is gearing up to host the India International Science Festival in Pune in December. Announcing this on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Union Minister of Science Jitendra Singh said at a press briefing that the government had taken a conscious decision to replace “scattered, repetitive gatherings”, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in October saw 13 Ministries and Nobel Laureates, and was an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, the India International Science Festival (IISF) brought a “festive, public-facing character with international resonance”. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 11:15:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has reconstituted a 10-member group that works on promoting science, technology and innovation toward achieving its Sustainable Development Goals. The lone Indian in this group is former biologist and former Council of Scientific and Industrial Research CSIR Director General, Shekhar Mande, who is also currently President, Indian National Science Academy. The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, while preparing for the 2027 SDG Summit. “The group comprises distinguished experts from diverse geographic and disciplinary backgrounds from both developing and developed countries. Each member, recognised for their international excellence in science or technology, brings a wealth of experience and insight from civil society, the private sector, and the scientific community, underscoring the inclusive and comprehensive approach the UN is taking towards sustainable development,” an accompanying press statement noted. The other members of the group are Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana), Deputy Director-General of CSIR Ghana; Giorgio Rossi (Italy), Vice-President of Elettra-Sincrotrone Trieste; Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Associate Professor at Malmö University; Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Professor at the Federal University of Campina Grande; Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russia), Member of the Civic Chamber of the Russian Federation; Motoko Kotani (Japan), Executive Director of Science at RIKEN; Jin Li (China), President of Fudan University; Madin Maseeh (Maldives), President of the Maldives Space Research Organisation; and Rita Orji (Nigeria), Canada Research Chair in Persuasive Technology at Dalhousie University. Professor Mande is also President of Vijnana Bharti, which, along with the Ministry of Science and Technology is gearing up to host the India International Science Festival in Pune in December. Announcing this on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Union Minister of Science Jitendra Singh said at a press briefing that the government had taken a conscious decision to replace “scattered, repetitive gatherings”, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in October saw 13 Ministries and Nobel Laureates, and was an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, the India International Science Festival (IISF) brought a “festive, public-facing character with international resonance”. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Inclusive (Adjective)
समावेशी — जिसमें समाज के हर वर्ग (खासकर गरीब और वंचित वर्ग) को बराबर शामिल किया जाए।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Egalitarian, All-encompassing  |  ✖ Ant: Exclusive, Discriminatory, Narrow
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
International (Adjective)
अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'UN Sustainable Development Goals group for scien' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'UN Sustainable Development Goals group for sc' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'UN Sustainable Development Goals group for sc' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The group has been constituted even as the international community ramps up efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development." (Hinglish Arth: इस समूह का गठन तब किया गया है जब अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समुदाय सतत विकास के लिए 2030 एजेंडा को प्राप्त करने के प्रयासों में तेजी ला रहा है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "UN Sustainable Development Goals group for science, technology rejigged"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the..." (Hinglish Arth: चंडीगढ़, हैदराबाद, गोवा और दिल्ली के बाद आयोजन स्थल को विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में घुमाकर, आईआईएसएफ को पहली बार पुणे में लाने से पश्चिमी केंद्र के जीवंत शैक्षणिक, अनुसंधान और औद्योगिक पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र का लाभ मिलता है।)

articles.title: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary as unrest grows over Hasina's return
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh ‌stepped up security and deployed hundreds of paramilitary troops nationwide on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) ​as the planned return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has ⁠sparked clashes, bomb blasts, and arson attacks blamed on supporters of her banned party. Ms. Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent protests demanding ‌her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card, saying she plans to return in December. But the government ‌has so far rejected her request, leading to members and supporters of ‌her ⁠Awami League party taking to the streets in protest. Last week, the party ⁠announced a week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support for Ms. Hasina's return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19. Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported. Late on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest ‌near Ms. Hasina's home district of Gopalganj, police said. On the same night, a ​crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and ⁠shops belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added. On Wednesday (November 18, 2026) morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district ‌of Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, authorities said. Tuesday (November 17, 2026) marked the day on which Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death a year ago by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising against her in 2024.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 37 Grameen Bank branches and offices have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires ‌since November 10, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), the bank said.

Ms. Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent protests demanding ‌her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card, saying she plans to return in December. But the government ‌has so far rejected her request, leading to members and supporters of ‌her ⁠Awami League party taking to the streets in protest. Last week, the party ⁠announced a week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support for Ms. Hasina's return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19. Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported. Late on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest ‌near Ms. Hasina's home district of Gopalganj, police said. On the same night, a ​crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and ⁠shops belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added. On Wednesday (November 18, 2026) morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district ‌of Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, authorities said. Tuesday (November 17, 2026) marked the day on which Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death a year ago by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising against her in 2024.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 37 Grameen Bank branches and offices have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires ‌since November 10, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), the bank said.

articles.title: Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saudi Arabia is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year, doubling down despite setbacks on the battlefield in Yemen ​and attacks disrupting life at home, said two Western officials briefed by Saudis on the plans. The renewed conflict has become the most active front in ‌the wider Iran war, killing and wounding thousands and displacing hundreds of thousands in Yemen while derailing ​Saudi Arabia's efforts to draw in non-oil investment and host global events. Public messaging around the war has also ⁠slowly shifted in the kingdom, with greater acknowledgement of its impacts. Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, aiming to see gains on the ground by the kingdom's Yemeni allies before any negotiations with the Houthis, according to Western officials, who spoke on condition ‌of anonymity to discuss non-public conversations with Saudi counterparts. A third source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts. All three said a deal to end the wider Iran war could see the Yemen conflict draw down. The ‌third source also said Riyadh believes that U.S. offensive support for Saudi operations in Yemen, which President Donald Trump's administration has ‌so ⁠far withheld, could help change the tide of the conflict, potentially allowing Saudi-backed forces to make the gains ⁠they want within weeks. A Saudi Foreign Ministry official declined to comment on the views of Saudi officials as described by the Western officials. Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen's government to power after the Houthis seized the ​capital Sanaa and much of the country. They fought to ‌a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year. Since fighting restarted, the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast and strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait from Saudi-backed forces, and encircled the city of Taiz in highlands above the government's temporary capital Aden on the southern coast.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect Aden in a major setback.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:55:36 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saudi Arabia is preparing for war against Yemen's Houthis to stretch well into next year, doubling down despite setbacks on the battlefield in Yemen ​and attacks disrupting life at home, said two Western officials briefed by Saudis on the plans. The renewed conflict has become the most active front in ‌the wider Iran war, killing and wounding thousands and displacing hundreds of thousands in Yemen while derailing ​Saudi Arabia's efforts to draw in non-oil investment and host global events. Public messaging around the war has also ⁠slowly shifted in the kingdom, with greater acknowledgement of its impacts. Saudi officials now foresee the campaign stretching on for up to six months, aiming to see gains on the ground by the kingdom's Yemeni allies before any negotiations with the Houthis, according to Western officials, who spoke on condition ‌of anonymity to discuss non-public conversations with Saudi counterparts. A third source familiar with the Saudi plans confirmed the accounts. All three said a deal to end the wider Iran war could see the Yemen conflict draw down. The ‌third source also said Riyadh believes that U.S. offensive support for Saudi operations in Yemen, which President Donald Trump's administration has ‌so ⁠far withheld, could help change the tide of the conflict, potentially allowing Saudi-backed forces to make the gains ⁠they want within weeks. A Saudi Foreign Ministry official declined to comment on the views of Saudi officials as described by the Western officials. Saudi Arabia first entered the Yemen conflict in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to try to restore Yemen's government to power after the Houthis seized the ​capital Sanaa and much of the country. They fought to ‌a bloody stalemate and in 2022 reached a ceasefire that lasted until summer this year. Since fighting restarted, the Houthis have seized the Red Sea coast and strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait from Saudi-backed forces, and encircled the city of Taiz in highlands above the government's temporary capital Aden on the southern coast.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Yemeni government forces mounted a counterattack last month, recapturing territory around the ‌strait, but withdrew over the past weekend to protect Aden in a major setback.

articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals. The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there. Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this. Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes. Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea. Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops. Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes. Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles). The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 that killed tens of thousands of people. The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:53:13 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Ethiopia and Eritrea have amassed forces along their shared border, conflict monitors and people tied to militias in northern Ethiopia's Tigray ‌region said, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals. The build-up along the border has brought ​the two armies within striking distance of each other, according to the conflict monitors ACLED and the International ⁠Crisis Group, a person close to a pro-Ethiopian government militia in Tigray, and another person close to anti-government rebels there. Reuters could not independently confirm reports of skirmishes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces along the border. ACLED and a person close to the rebels said the ‌two sides had clashed in recent days, which would be their first direct armed exchanges in over a month, but the person close to the pro-Ethiopian government militia disputed this. Reached for comment, Eritrean Information ‌Minister Yemane Gebremeskel decried "propaganda" from Ethiopia's ruling party about developments near the border but did not directly address reports about ‌military ⁠build-ups or clashes. Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Diplomats and ⁠experts have warned of possible conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea since fighting broke out in September between Ethiopia’s federal government and rebels in Tigray, which borders Eritrea. Witnesses and Ethiopia's government said Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October in support ​of the rebels. ACLED reported at the time ‌that drone strikes it believed were carried out by Ethiopia’s military had targeted the Eritrean troops. Ethiopia has not commented on the strikes. Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles). The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 that killed tens of thousands of people. The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Independence (Adjective / Verb)
स्वतंत्रता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Independence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Information (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Information' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

A. The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, hei' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Eritrea has denied any incursion into Ethiopia and accused Addis Ababa of seeking a pretext to invade its smaller neighbour, which was an Ethiopian province for three decades before gaining independence in 1993. They are now separated ‌by a border stretching more than 1,000 km (620 miles). The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels. Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt ⁠all deny doing so.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ethiopia and Eritrea fought a border war from 1998 to 2000 that killed tens of thousands of people. The conflict was prompted by a dispute over the border town of Badme, which a UN boundary commission later found fell within Eritrean ‌territory.

articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The body overseeing U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza ‌war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving ​the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse. The 12-page Board ⁠of Peace report, seen by Reuters , is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the U.S.-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then. The Board, established and headed by Mr. Trump, is expected ‌to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November. "The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains ‌the principal risk to the process," the report said, warning that "a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be ‌sustained ⁠indefinitely." While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year. Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected ​the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas ‌is dismantled. Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops. "Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said. "Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not ‌been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Senior Hamas ​official Basem Naim dismissed the report as "pure disinformation", accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to ⁠continue its aggression in Gaza.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (18 NOV)

📰 Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war

📌 Published: 18 Nov 2026, 10:51:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The body overseeing U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza ‌war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving ​the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse. The 12-page Board ⁠of Peace report, seen by Reuters , is the body's second to the United Nations Security Council since the U.S.-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then. The Board, established and headed by Mr. Trump, is expected ‌to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November. "The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains ‌the principal risk to the process," the report said, warning that "a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be ‌sustained ⁠indefinitely." While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year. Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected ​the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas ‌is dismantled. Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops. "Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said. "Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not ‌been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Senior Hamas ​official Basem Naim dismissed the report as "pure disinformation", accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to ⁠continue its aggression in Gaza.
